headline: You refine frontend experiences through precise corrections, accessible interactions, and practical engineering tradeoffs—often well after midnight.

archetype.name: The Midnight UI Refiner
archetype.description: You work in short feedback loops, spotting the spacing, browser behavior, or missing keyboard interaction that needs attention next. Your prompts combine concrete implementation choices with a persistent concern for how interfaces feel and function. When an approach keeps resisting, you choose a workable fallback and keep moving.

dimensions.title: Small steps, explicit checks
dimensions.summary: You steer implementation through compact requests and precise adjustments. You also use measurable quality targets and accept practical fallbacks when further effort has diminishing returns.

evidence.quote: 不對，間距太大了，gap 改成 12px
幫我寫個 script 檢查所有 token 組合的對比度
好，那先用原生 img，我之後再處理

dimensions.title: Brief and technically specific
dimensions.summary: You communicate in concise Traditional Chinese with English technical terms woven in. Your corrections usually identify the exact mismatch, and your acknowledgments often lead directly into the next refinement.

evidence.quote: 錯了，category 是陣列，不是字串
可以了，謝謝，順便幫我把按鈕的 disabled 樣式調一下

dimensions.title: Frontend depth, browser awareness
dimensions.summary: Your work spans React data fetching, form validation, reusable components, and Next.js constraints. You bring your own browser and rendering diagnoses, giving the assistant specific technical hypotheses to work from.

evidence.quote: 幫我寫一個 useProducts hook，支援分頁跟 category filter

dimensions.title: Polish that stays usable
dimensions.summary: You pay attention to shadows, loading states, animation, and typography. Accessibility recurs alongside that visual work through contrast, reduced motion, accessible names, and keyboard focus.

evidence.quote: 陰影太重了，淡一點，像 tailwind 的 shadow-sm

dimensions.title: Turn recurring fixes into guardrails
dimensions.summary: You already show a move toward reusable quality controls through contrast scripts, design tokens, and component stories. A useful next step would be to bring your recurring accessibility and interaction requirements into initial acceptance criteria, reducing the need to add them during correction rounds.

traits.name: Precision through iteration
traits.description: You refine working details with explicit values and follow-up requirements, keeping feedback immediately actionable.

traits.description: You repeatedly catch usability requirements across visual design, motion, forms, and keyboard interaction.

traits.name: Pragmatic about tradeoffs
traits.description: You persist with problems but can change tactics, simplify an implementation, or defer work when a fallback gets you moving.

traits.name: An active debugging partner
traits.description: You challenge incorrect diagnoses and contribute specific causes, keeping the assistant anchored to the actual browser behavior.

funFacts: Your latest recorded prompt landed at 02:36 in Asia/Taipei—late-night UI tuning has receipts.
You wrote 51 prompts across 12 sessions and 12 active days.
Your median prompt length was 27 characters: compact requests are your usual format.
Your recorded correction rate was 19.61%; you regularly steer the assistant back on course.
Your project split was 43 prompts for shop-web and 8 for portfolio.
